b: The British colony of the Gold Coast became the independent state of Ghana under Prime Minister Kwame Nkrumah. It was the first colony in sub-Saharan Africa to gain independence from European rule.
sig: It inspired independence movements across the continent.

b: Kenya became independent from Britain after the Mau Mau uprising and a state of emergency that lasted from 1952 to 1960. Jomo Kenyatta led the new government and became president when Kenya turned republic in 1964.
sig: It ended decades of colonial rule in East Africa’s largest settler colony.

b: Six British colonies joined to form the Commonwealth of Australia, with a federal parliament and constitution. Indigenous Australians were largely excluded from the founding political settlement.
sig: It created the modern Australian federal state.

b: The British North America Act united the Province of Canada, split into Ontario and Quebec, with Nova Scotia and New Brunswick as a federal dominion. More provinces and territories joined over the following decades.
sig: It is commemorated each year as Canada Day.

t: The Declaration of Independence at Tucumán
b: Delegates at the Congress of Tucumán declared the independence of the United Provinces of the Río de la Plata from Spain. Years of war and civil conflict followed before a stable Argentine state emerged.

t: The Kingdom of Italy is proclaimed
b: After the campaigns of Garibaldi and the diplomacy of Cavour, Victor Emmanuel II was proclaimed king of a united Italy. Venetia joined in 1866 and Rome in 1871 to complete the unification.
sig: It ended centuries of political fragmentation on the peninsula.

b: A Parisian crowd attacked the Bastille fortress-prison, seeking weapons and gunpowder amid political crisis. The event became a symbol of the French Revolution.
The Nasrid emirate of Granada surrendered to the Catholic Monarchs, Isabella of Castile and Ferdinand of Aragon. It ended Muslim rule on the Iberian Peninsula after nearly eight centuries.
sig: The same year Spain sponsored Columbus’s first voyage.
